stem: What is the main function of the skull?

options.rationale: Movement of the head happens at joints in the neck.

options.content: To store calcium for the teeth
options.rationale: This is not its main function.
The skull surrounds and protects the brain.
The ribcage protects the lungs.

explanation: The skull is a case of fused bones that protects the brain (and the eyes and ears).
hints: What organ does the skull surround?

stem: Which bone is found in the upper arm?

options.rationale: The humerus is the single bone of the upper arm.
The femur is the thigh bone.
The radius is in the forearm.
The scapula is the shoulder blade.

explanation: The humerus runs from the shoulder to the elbow. The forearm contains the radius and ulna.
hints: It runs from the shoulder to the elbow.

stem: True or false: muscles can only pull; they cannot push.

answerSpec.feedbackTrue: Correct. That is why muscles work in antagonistic pairs.
answerSpec.feedbackFalse: It is true. A muscle can only contract and pull; another muscle must pull the bone back.

explanation: Muscles produce force only when they contract (shorten). They cannot push, so a second, antagonistic muscle is needed to move the bone back.
hints: What does a muscle do when it works?

stem: What type of joint is the hip joint?

options.rationale: The knee and elbow are hinge joints.
The head of the femur fits into a socket in the pelvic girdle.
The hip moves freely.

options.content: Gliding joint between the skull bones
options.rationale: Skull bones are joined by fixed joints.

explanation: The hip is a ball-and-socket joint: the rounded head of the femur fits into a cup-shaped socket in the pelvic girdle, allowing movement in all directions.
hints: The leg can swing forwards, backwards and sideways at the hip.

stem: Name the tough, inelastic tissue that joins a muscle to a bone.

rejected.feedback: Cartilage covers the ends of bones at joints.
The synovial membrane makes synovial fluid.

explanation: Tendons join muscles to bones. Because they are inelastic, they pass the full pull of a contracting muscle to the bone.
hints: It is not a ligament.

stem: Match each bone with its description.

right.content: The bone of the upper arm
The larger bone of the lower leg (the shin bone)
The hip bones, which the legs are attached to
The forearm bone on the thumb side

explanation: Scapula: shoulder blade. Humerus: upper arm. Femur: thigh. Tibia: shin. Pelvic girdle: hip bones. The forearm bone on the thumb side is the radius.
hints: One description belongs to the radius.

stem: Which list gives three main functions of the skeleton?

options.rationale: These are carried out by other organ systems.
The skeleton does not digest food.
Animals do not photosynthesise.
These are the three main functions.

explanation: The skeleton supports the body and gives it shape, protects delicate organs, and allows movement by providing levers that muscles pull on at joints.
hints: Think about the skull, the ribcage and the limbs.

stem: Which statement about ligaments and tendons is correct?

options.content: Ligaments join bone to bone and are slightly elastic; tendons join muscle to bone and are inelastic.
options.rationale: This lets joints move while tendons pass on the full pull of muscles.

options.content: Ligaments join muscle to bone and are inelastic; tendons join bone to bone and are elastic.
options.rationale: This is the wrong way round.

options.content: Both ligaments and tendons are very elastic.
options.rationale: Tendons must be inelastic to pass on the pull of muscles.
Tendons are made of tough fibrous tissue.

explanation: Ligaments hold bones together at joints; being slightly elastic, they allow movement. Tendons attach muscles to bones; being inelastic, they transmit the full pull of the muscle to the bone.
hints: Tendons connect muscle to bone.

stem: What happens to the biceps and triceps when the arm is bent at the elbow?

options.rationale: If both contracted together, the arm would not move.

options.content: The biceps relaxes and the triceps contracts.
options.rationale: This straightens the arm.

options.content: The biceps contracts and the triceps relaxes.
options.rationale: The biceps pulls the radius up.
Movement needs a muscle to contract.

explanation: To bend the arm, the biceps (the flexor) contracts and pulls the radius upwards, while the triceps (the extensor) relaxes and is stretched.
hints: The biceps is on the front of the upper arm.

stem: What is the function of the cartilage that covers the ends of the bones at a movable joint?

options.content: To attach the muscles firmly to the ends of the bones
options.rationale: Tendons do this.

options.content: To reduce friction between the bones and absorb shocks
options.rationale: Smooth cartilage lets the bones move easily.
The synovial membrane makes synovial fluid.
Ligaments do this.

explanation: Cartilage is smooth and slightly springy. It stops the bones rubbing together, reducing friction and wear, and it absorbs shocks, for example when we land after a jump.
hints: Think about two bone ends moving against each other.

stem: What is the role of synovial fluid in a movable joint?

options.content: It joins the muscles to the bones.
options.rationale: Tendons do this.

options.content: It carries oxygen and glucose to the muscles around the joint.
options.rationale: This is not its role.
Ligaments do this.

options.content: It lubricates the joint so that the bones move smoothly.
options.rationale: It acts like oil in a machine.

explanation: Synovial fluid, made by the synovial membrane, lubricates the joint, reducing friction so that the bones move smoothly over each other.
hints: Think about oil in a machine.

stem: Complete the sentences about the leg.

payload.template: The thigh bone is the {{blank:fem}}. The two bones of the lower leg are the tibia and the {{blank:fib}}. The knee is a {{blank:joint}} joint.

explanation: The femur is the thigh bone; the tibia and fibula form the lower leg; the knee is a hinge joint, allowing bending and straightening.
hints: The lower-arm bones are the radius and ulna; the lower-leg bones are different.

stem: Why do skeletal muscles work in antagonistic pairs?

options.content: Each muscle can only contract for a short time, so the two muscles take turns.
options.rationale: Antagonistic muscles produce opposite movements, not the same movement in turns.

options.content: Two muscles are needed to push the bone.
options.rationale: Muscles cannot push.

options.content: One muscle makes the energy and the other uses it.
options.rationale: Each muscle respires to release its own energy.

options.content: A muscle can only pull, so a second muscle is needed to move the bone back.
options.rationale: Each muscle of the pair produces the opposite movement.

explanation: Muscles can only contract and pull. When one muscle has bent a joint, it cannot straighten it again; its antagonist must contract to pull the bone back, stretching the first muscle.
hints: Can a muscle push?

stem: Which of these is a hinge joint?

options.rationale: The hip is a ball-and-socket joint.
The shoulder is a ball-and-socket joint.
The knee bends and straightens in one plane, like a hinge.

options.content: The joints between the bones of the skull
options.rationale: These are fixed joints.

explanation: The knee (and the elbow) are hinge joints, allowing movement in one plane only. The hip and shoulder are ball-and-socket joints; the joints of the skull are fixed.
hints: Which joint can only bend and straighten?

stem: True or false: tendons are inelastic, so the pull of a contracting muscle is passed directly to the bone.

answerSpec.feedbackTrue: Correct. A stretchy tendon would waste some of the pull.
answerSpec.feedbackFalse: It is true. Tendons do not stretch, so all the pull of the muscle moves the bone.

explanation: If tendons stretched, some of the muscle's pull would be used stretching the tendon instead of moving the bone. Inelastic tendons pass on the full force.
hints: What would happen if a tendon stretched like an elastic band?

options.rationale: The biceps contracts to bend the arm.
The triceps is the extensor; it straightens the arm.
If both contracted, the arm would not move.
Bones are moved by muscles.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Describe how muscles E and F straighten the arm.

points.description: F (triceps) contracts / shortens
E (biceps) relaxes and is stretched
F pulls on D (the ulna) through its tendon, so the forearm moves down / the arm straightens at the elbow

parts.stem: Explain why E and F are described as antagonistic muscles.

points.description: They produce opposite movements at the same joint: when one contracts the other relaxes

Muscles can only pull.

stem: The knee is a movable joint. Inside it, the ends of the femur and tibia are covered by a smooth layer, the joint is lined by a membrane that makes a fluid, and tough bands hold the bones together.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Match each part of the knee joint with its function.

right.content: Reduces friction between the bone ends and absorbs shocks
Hold the bones together at the joint
Joins the thigh muscles to the bone

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: In some older people, the cartilage in the knee wears away. Suggest why their knees become painful and stiff.

points.description: Without cartilage the bones rub against each other / there is more friction
Bone ends are damaged / inflamed, causing pain and making movement difficult

parts.explanation: Without cartilage, the ends of the femur and tibia rub directly against each other, so there is much more friction. The bone surfaces become damaged and inflamed, which is painful and makes the knee stiff.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Which pair of muscles bends and straightens the knee?

options.rationale: These move the elbow.
The hamstrings are the flexors; the quadriceps are the extensors.
These move the ribs.
These are used in breathing.

explanation: Cartilage reduces friction and absorbs shocks; synovial fluid lubricates; ligaments hold the bones together. Worn cartilage lets bone rub on bone, causing pain and stiffness. The hamstrings bend the knee and the quadriceps straighten it.
hints: Which part stops bone rubbing on bone?

stem: Describe the functions of the skeleton, giving an example of each. [6]

points.description: Support: framework that gives the body its shape / holds organs in place
Example of support, e.g. the vertebral column holds the body upright / bones provide attachment for muscles
Protection of delicate organs
Example of protection, e.g. skull protects the brain / ribcage protects the heart and lungs / vertebral column protects the spinal cord
Movement / locomotion: muscles pull on bones, which act as levers at joints
Example of movement, e.g. biceps and triceps moving the forearm at the elbow / legs moving at the hip and knee in walking

answerSpec.modelAnswer: The skeleton supports the body: it is a rigid framework that gives the body its shape, holds the organs in place and provides surfaces for muscles to attach to; for example, the vertebral column holds the body upright. It protects delicate organs: the skull protects the brain, the ribcage protects the heart and lungs, and the vertebral column protects the spinal cord. It also allows movement: muscles attached to bones by tendons pull on them, and the bones act as levers moving at joints; for example, the biceps and triceps move the forearm at the elbow, and the leg muscles move the femur at the hip during walking.

explanation: The three functions are support, protection and movement; each needs a named example.
hints: Give one example for each of the three functions.

stem: Explain how the biceps and triceps produce movement at the elbow joint, and why two muscles are needed rather than one. [6]

points.description: Muscles are attached to bones by (inelastic) tendons
Biceps contracts / shortens and pulls the radius, bending (flexing) the arm
while the triceps relaxes (and is stretched)
Triceps contracts and pulls the ulna, straightening (extending) the arm, while the biceps relaxes
The elbow is a hinge joint, so movement is in one plane (the elbow acts as a pivot / the forearm as a lever)
Muscles can only pull (contract), not push
So a second (antagonistic) muscle is needed to reverse the movement / stretch the relaxed muscle

answerSpec.modelAnswer: The biceps and triceps are attached to the bones by inelastic tendons. To bend the arm, the biceps contracts and shortens, pulling on the radius so that the forearm rises about the elbow, which acts as the pivot of a lever; at the same time the triceps relaxes and is stretched. To straighten the arm, the triceps contracts and pulls on the ulna while the biceps relaxes. The elbow is a hinge joint, so these movements are in one plane. Two muscles are needed because a muscle can only pull: once the biceps has bent the arm it cannot push it straight again, so the triceps, its antagonist, must contract to reverse the movement and stretch the biceps.

explanation: The biceps (flexor) and triceps (extensor) are an antagonistic pair. Each can only pull, so one bends the elbow and the other straightens it.
hints: Describe bending and straightening separately.
End with why one muscle could not do both.

stem: The arm and the leg are built on the same plan. Which bone of the leg corresponds in position to the humerus of the arm?

options.rationale: The tibia corresponds to one of the forearm bones.
The pelvic girdle corresponds to the shoulder girdle (scapula).
The fibula corresponds to one of the forearm bones.
Each is the single long bone nearest the body.

explanation: Both limbs follow the plan girdle → one bone → two bones → many small bones. The femur (thigh) corresponds to the humerus (upper arm); the tibia and fibula correspond to the radius and ulna.
hints: The humerus is the single bone nearest the shoulder.

stem: Which bone forms the point of the elbow?

options.rationale: The radius is on the thumb side of the forearm.
The end of the ulna forms the bony point of the elbow.
The humerus meets the forearm bones at the elbow, but the point is formed by the ulna.
The scapula is at the shoulder.

explanation: The upper end of the ulna forms the point of the elbow; the triceps is attached to it.
hints: It is the forearm bone on the little-finger side.

The table shows typical maximum ranges of movement at four joints of an adult.

| Joint | Bending forwards and back | Moving out to the side | Rotation (turning) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Elbow | 145° | 0° | 0° |
| Knee | 135° | 0° | 0° (when straight) |
| Shoulder | 180° | 180° | 90° |
| Hip | 120° | 45° | 45° |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which two joints are ball-and-socket joints?

options.rationale: These move in one plane only: they are hinge joints.
The elbow moves in one plane only.
Both move in several directions, including rotation.
The knee moves in one plane only.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Explain how the data support your answer to (a).

points.description: The shoulder and hip move in several planes (forwards and back, to the side) and can rotate
whereas the elbow and knee move only forwards and back (one plane), like a hinge

parts.explanation: The shoulder and hip can bend forwards and back, move out to the side and rotate, so they move in all directions. The elbow and knee move only forwards and back, in one plane, like a door hinge.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: How much greater, in degrees, is the forwards-and-back range of the shoulder than that of the hip?

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: The hip has a smaller range of movement than the shoulder. Suggest why this is an advantage.

points.description: The head of the femur sits in a deep socket in the pelvic girdle / is held by strong ligaments
making the hip more stable / less likely to dislocate when it supports the weight of the body

parts.explanation: The head of the femur fits deeply into its socket in the pelvic girdle and is held by strong ligaments. This limits movement but makes the hip very stable, so it can support the body's weight without dislocating.

explanation: The shoulder and hip move in several planes and rotate, so they are ball-and-socket joints; the elbow and knee are hinge joints. The shoulder's range is $180 - 120 = 60°$ greater. The hip trades range for stability, because it carries the body's weight.
hints: A hinge moves in one plane only.
Which joint has to support the weight of the body?
